section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah, which involves descent into physical and impure matters yet remains Torah, and refinement through the inner dimension of Torah, which operates without such descent.
section.t: Now, in the refinement through Torah, there is a distinction between the refinement that comes through the revealed aspect of Torah and the refinement that comes through the inner dimension of Torah21.
For in the refinement through the study of the revealed aspect of Torah, the study must be in those matters that need to be refined,
and the reason for this is that the Torah was clothed in physical matters and also in forbidden things, even in the claims of falsehood22,
it is,
in order to effect refinement also in these matters23.
And that even the refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah is called refinement in a manner of rest24
is because even these matters
(forbidden things and even claims of falsehood)
as they are in the Torah25,
are Torah,
Torah of truth,
and since even these things in the Torah are the word of G-d26,
"Behold, My word is like fire"27,
just as fire etc., so too the words of Torah do not receive impurity28,
thus the Torah is always in its place and level
(the word of G-d),
and the refinement is in a manner of automatic.
However, even so, this is not comparable to the refinement through the inner dimension of Torah,
for in the refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah, the very fact that the Torah speaks about physical matters etc.,
this is a matter of descent29
as it were,
except that even after its descent and drawing down below, it is Torah,
the word of G-d
(and it does not descend and become clothed in something else).
In contrast, the refinement through the inner dimension of Torah,
since the inner dimension of Torah is the Tree of Life
(which is not clothed in good and evil)30,
the refinement accomplished through it is not in a manner of clothing at all.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that true rest and peace are found specifically in the inner dimension of Torah, where there are no questions or disputes, unlike the revealed aspect which involves questions and refutations.
section.t: And perhaps one may add to the distinction between the revealed aspect of Torah and the inner dimension of Torah,
that the true essence of rest and peace is specifically in the inner dimension of Torah,
not only in the matter of refinements through the study of Torah,
but also in the study of Torah itself.
For the study of the revealed aspect of Torah is in a manner of questions and answers,
where at first one assumes that the reasoning is such and such,
and afterwards one arrives at a deeper understanding and rejects the previous reasoning,
even saying of it that it is nonsense31.
For the rejection of the previous reasoning is a matter of "you have shed much blood"
(said regarding Dovid32)
as it is in the world of intellect.
And the true matter of peace is specifically in the inner dimension of Torah,
where there is no question nor dispute33.
And it can be said,
that this distinction between the revealed aspect of Torah and the inner dimension of Torah in the manner of study itself,
is the cause of the distinction between them in the matter of refinement through them,
for every effect acts in its own likeness,
and therefore,
specifically the inner dimension of Torah,
in which itself there is no question nor dispute,
also the refinement through it is in a manner of peace and rest.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section describes two levels within the inner dimension of Torah: one grasped by intellect, subject to doubt, and the other perceived through vision, which is immutable and becomes part of one's essence.
section.t: Now, even within the inner dimension of Torah itself, there are two general modes.
As it is clothed in the understanding and comprehension of the intellect,
for this level of the inner dimension of Torah exists even now,
and as it is in the aspect of vision
(above understanding and comprehension),
which level will be in the future,
as is known34
that Mashiach will teach
(the inner dimension)
of the Torah to all of Israel in a manner of vision.
And the difference between comprehension and vision is,
that in comprehension,
even when it is in truth,
it is possible that through a question there will be a change or at least a weakening in him.
In contrast, in vision,
even if the strongest questions are posed to him,
he will have no doubt whatsoever in what he saw.
And the reason for this is,
that when a person comprehends something with his intellect,
it is something additional to him,
in contrast, when he sees something,
the thing is engraved in his innermost being and as if it becomes a part of his very self, and therefore change is not applicable to it.
